events.objective: Establish the true onset time and blast radius. For the window 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z to 11:59:00Z, characterize api-gateway p99 latency and 504 rate over time to pin the onset minute; then determine which services actually show degradation (error rate, latency, saturation) in that same window, especially any services behind /v1/portfolio/* (portfolio, positions, pricing, market-data, auth, downstream DBs/caches). Identify error signatures (timeouts, connection resets, pool exhaustion, upstream 5xx vs gateway 504) and whether anomalies begin before or after the gateway latency rises. Report per-service evidence so we can distinguish gateway-as-cause from gateway-as-victim.

Inventory what changed today and the dependency topology. List all deployments and config changes on 2026-03-10 (all services, not just api-gateway) with timestamps, focusing on the gateway HTTP/2 upstream upgrade and anything touching portfolio-path services. Map service dependencies for the /v1/portfolio/* call path (gateway -> upstreams -> datastores) to find shared components and fan-out. Separately, search historical incidents for past gateway p99/504 spikes or HTTP/2 upgrade incidents and their causes/resolutions, to see whether this pattern was previously caused by the gateway or by a downstream service.

Correlate changes against the onset time from task a. Determine whether the change-inventory events (deployment/config timestamps from task b) align with the onset minute: does the gateway upgrade land just before onset, or do other changes (or no change) align better? Judge whether the timing supports the gateway-upgrade hypothesis or points to an independent/downstream trigger, and identify any change to a shared component that precedes symptoms across multiple services.

events.statement: Exactly one deployment was recorded on 2026-03-10 across all services: api-gateway v9.3.0 at 08:00:00Z, 'Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams', with changes 'envoy 1.29 -> 1.30' and 'upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service', author platform-team, status 'live', rolled_back_at null.

A second, non-gateway change landed at 09:52:00Z on portfolio-service: db.pool.max_size reduced from 50 to 5 by infra-automation, description 'Apply cost-optimisation profile 'small' to service datasource'. This is ~1h52m after the gateway deploy and 13 minutes before the 10:05Z report.

Only two config changes exist for 2026-03-10 in total: cfg-2199 (order-service log.sampling_rate 0.1→0.2 at 07:00:00Z) and cfg-2207 (portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50→5 at 09:52:00Z). No other service had a config change.

The /v1/portfolio/* fan-out is: api-gateway → portfolio-service; portfolio-service → ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache); market-data-service → redis-cache (cache) and exchange-gateway (http). ledger-db and redis-cache are marked shared=true.

ledger-db is shared across the portfolio path and other services: order-service → ledger-db, payment-service → ledger-db, portfolio-service → ledger-db; redis-cache is shared by auth-service, portfolio-service and market-data-service.

Historical incidents contain precedents for the same symptom from BOTH sides. Gateway-side: HIST-116 (2025-12-18) 'HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade', symptoms '504 at gateway','upstream resets','timeouts', root cause 'Envoy upgrade changed HTTP/2 max concurrent streams default', resolution 'Rolled back gateway', match_score 5. Downstream/shared-datastore: HIST-102 (2025-09-02) 'Portfolio timeouts during ledger-db failover', symptoms 'portfolio page timeouts','504 at gateway', root cause 'Unplanned ledger-db primary failover' (match_score 4); HIST-115 (2025-09-25) order-service pool exhaustion from 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', category config_change.

Both changes touching the portfolio path (dep-5220 at 08:00Z and cfg-2207 at 09:52Z) precede the 10:05:00Z incident report, and neither the gateway deploy nor any deployment shows a rollback (rolled_back_at null; only one deployment returned for the 2026-03-09→2026-03-10 window).

events.answer: On 2026-03-10 two changes were recorded across all services: api-gateway v9.3.0 (envoy 1.29→1.30, enabling HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service) at 08:00:00Z and never rolled back, and a portfolio-service config change (db.pool.max_size 50→5, "cost-optimisation profile 'small'") at 09:52:00Z. events.statement: api-gateway p99 latency was flat and healthy (~200-210ms avg, max ≤231ms) from 08:00 through the 09:45 bucket, then jumped to avg 1849.99ms / max 4418.76ms in the 09:50 bucket and stayed elevated at ~4260-4420ms avg (max up to 4711.85ms) through 11:55. This pins the gateway latency onset to the 09:45-09:50 transition (one 5-minute bucket boundary), well AFTER the 08:00 start of the window.

api-gateway error_rate (HTTP 5xx % of requests) was stable at ~0.17-0.28% from 08:00 through 09:45, then jumped to avg 1.66% / max 7.18% in the 09:50 bucket and held at ~7.0-7.5% through 11:55. The error onset coincides with the same 09:45→09:50 bucket as the latency jump, i.e. 504s/5xx begin in the same interval as the latency rise.

The gateway was healthy (p99 ~200ms, 5xx ~0.2%) for the first ~1h45m of the requested window (08:00-09:45) despite the gateway upgrade having reportedly shipped 'earlier today'. Degradation starts suddenly at ~09:47-09:50 rather than gradually, consistent with a discrete change or downstream failure at that minute, not a slow build.

query_logs for api-gateway over 08:00-11:59 with min_level=ERROR returned 0 matches ('total_matched': 0, returned 0, truncated false) even though gateway error_rate was ~7% during 09:50-11:59. The gateway log stream therefore has no ERROR-level entries despite ~7% 5xx, so gateway error signatures (upstream 5xx vs 504) could not be extracted from logs in this window.

My five parallel queries for downstream services 'portfolio', 'pricing', 'market-data', 'positions' all failed with not_found; the error payload lists the real known services: 'portfolio-service', 'pricing-engine', 'market-data-service', 'auth-service', 'redis-cache', 'ledger-db', 'user-db', 'exchange-api', etc. So the downstream blast-radius queries were never run and NO downstream service has been confirmed healthy or degraded by me.

events.description: Downstream services were queried under wrong names (portfolio, pricing, market-data, positions) and 5 queries returned not_found; the remaining retry queries hit the tool-call budget. No per-service latency/error/saturation data was obtained for portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service, auth-service, positions-equivalent, ledger-db, redis-cache, user-db.

api-gateway ERROR logs returned zero entries for 08:00-11:59 despite ~7% 5xx; no log stream captured the gateway's error signatures (timeouts, connection resets, pool exhaustion, upstream 5xx vs gateway-generated 504).
Both on-set signals are in the same 300s bucket (09:45→09:50), so the ordering of gateway latency rise vs gateway 504 rise cannot be resolved at this resolution.

events.answer: api-gateway degraded abruptly at the 09:45→09:50 bucket boundary: p99 went from ~204ms (09:45) to avg 1850ms/max 4419ms (09:50) and settled at ~4300ms, while error_rate went from 0.21% (09:45) to avg 1.66%/max 7.18% (09:50) and settled at ~7.2%. The gateway was fully healthy for 08:00-09:45, so an upgrade supposedly shipped 'earlier today' did not cause an immediate failure. I could NOT establish blast radius: all downstream service queries failed on wrong service names and the corrected retries exhausted the tool budget, so no downstream service is confirmed degraded or healthy and the gateway-as-cause vs gateway-as-victim question remains open.

events.statement: The only deployment on 2026-03-10 (across all services) is api-gateway v9.3.0 dep-5220 at 08:00:00Z, 'Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams' (envoy 1.29->1.30, h2 for portfolio-service and order-service), status 'live', rolled_back_at null. This lands ~1h45m BEFORE the 09:45->09:50 onset boundary, and a wider sweep from 2026-03-09 onward returns the same single deployment.

The only config change on 2026-03-10 (all services) is cfg-2207 on portfolio-service: db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 at 09:52:00Z, author infra-automation, 'Apply cost-optimisation profile 'small' to service datasource'. It has no rollback recorded and is the single non-gateway change touching the /v1/portfolio/* path.

Timing verdict: neither change aligns exactly with the 09:45->09:50 onset bucket. The gateway deploy (08:00:00Z) precedes onset by ~1h47m and the gateway was healthy at p99 ~200ms / 5xx ~0.2% throughout 08:00-09:45, so the gateway upgrade did NOT land just before onset. The portfolio-service pool cut (09:52:00Z) lands ~2-5 min AFTER the first degraded bucket (09:50, p99 avg 1849.99ms / max 4418.76ms), i.e. after symptoms began.

/v1/portfolio/* topology: api-gateway -> portfolio-service -> {ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache)}; market-data-service -> {redis-cache, exchange-gateway}. Both ledger-db and redis-cache are marked shared=true, so a shared-component fault can produce portfolio-path symptoms independently of the gateway.

ledger-db is shared well beyond the portfolio path: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service all have db edges to ledger-db; api-gateway fronts order-service, portfolio-service and payment-service. A ledger-db fault would therefore precede/degrade symptoms across multiple services, not just the portfolio page.

Historical precedents exist for this exact symptom pattern from BOTH sides: HIST-116 (2025-12-18) 'HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade' with '504 at gateway', 'upstream resets', 'timeouts' from 'Envoy upgrade changed HTTP/2 max concurrent streams default' (match_score 5.0-5.5, bad_deployment); and HIST-102 (2025-09-02) 'Portfolio timeouts during ledger-db failover' with 'portfolio page timeouts','504 at gateway' from an unplanned ledger-db primary failover (match_score 4). HIST-115 is a pool-misconfiguration precedent ('Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', category config_change). These are leads only, not evidence of the current cause.

events.description: Could not query metrics for the shared components ledger-db and redis-cache: the redis-cache dependency call and the metric queries hit the tool budget, and T1 also showed downstream metric queries require exact service names ('ledger-db', 'redis-cache', not 'portfolio'). No ledger-db/redis-cache p99, error, connection or saturation data was obtained for 09:30-10:00.

No deployment or config event exists in the inventory at or within ~5 minutes of the 09:45-09:50 onset minute (only 08:00 deploy and 09:52 config), so no change event can be shown to mechanically align with onset.
No rollback events were observed for any service in the window (dep-5220 rolled_back_at null), so the effect of reverting either change on symptoms could not be assessed.

events.answer: Timing does NOT support the gateway-upgrade hypothesis as stated: dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0, HTTP/2 to upstreams) shipped at 08:00:00Z and the gateway stayed healthy (p99 ~200ms, 5xx ~0.2%) for ~1h45m until the abrupt 09:45->09:50 onset, so it did not land just before onset. No other change aligns at the onset minute either: the only other change, cfg-2207 (portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5), landed at 09:52:00Z, ~2-5 min AFTER the first degraded bucket. The change inventory therefore points away from a discrete pre-onset change and toward either a downstream/shared-component trigger (ledger-db or redis-cache, both shared=true and upstream of portfolio-service) or a delayed expression of a change; I could not confirm a shared-component fault.

tasks.answer: Timing does NOT support the gateway-upgrade hypothesis as stated: dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0, HTTP/2 to upstreams) shipped at 08:00:00Z and the gateway stayed healthy (p99 ~200ms, 5xx ~0.2%) for ~1h45m until the abrupt 09:45->09:50 onset, so it did not land just before onset. No other change aligns at the onset minute either: the only other change, cfg-2207 (portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5), landed at 09:52:00Z, ~2-5 min AFTER the first degraded bucket. The change inventory therefore points away from a discrete pre-onset change and toward either a downstream/shared-component trigger (ledger-db or redis-cache, both shared=true and upstream of portfolio-service) or a delayed expression of a change; I could not confirm a shared-component fault.
